title: generated papers merit a trial
description: INFOSYS co-founder Nandan Nilekani has suggested an innovative way to curb paper leaks. His proposal to use artificial intelligence (AI) to generate question papers on exam day offers a promising opportunity to reform a system desperately in need of credibility. Nilekani, who is heading a committee dedicated to systemic reforms, has argued that setting the papers from a vast question bank at the last minute could eliminate the commercial incentive behind paper leaks. His idea, coupled with a nationwide transition to computer-based testing, deserves serious consideration. However, technological innovation must be accompanied by institutional accountability and equal access. The logic behind AI-generated papers is compelling. If questions are selected securely just before a test, the possibility of advance access could be substantially reduced. Still, independent audits and human oversight will be essential to prevent errors, bias and manipulation.

title: 'Data centres must be seen as strategic infrastructure': Niti Aayog report
description: Niti Aayog has released a report urging states to consider data centres as strategic infrastructure. The report suggests a structured approach to developing data centres sustainably. It highlights the need for common standards and guidance from the central government to support growth. Additionally, the report emphasizes the importance of assessing local resources and economic benefits. This framework aims to strengthen India's data-centre sector and its artificial intelligence economy.
